definition: timm (PyTorch Image Models) is a large collection of pretrained vision backbones — ResNets, EfficientNets, ViTs, ConvNeXt — with one API.
details: Created by Ross Wightman in 2019; now maintained at Hugging Face.

explainer.lead: How to install timm, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.

quickstart.python:
import timm
import torch

model = timm.create_model("convnext_tiny", pretrained=True, num_classes=5)   # new 5-class head
features = timm.create_model("vit_small_patch16_224", pretrained=True, num_classes=0)
print(model(torch.randn(1, 3, 224, 224)).shape, features(torch.randn(1, 3, 224, 224)).shape)

explainer.inAi: Pick a backbone, set num_classes, and fine-tune it on your images; num_classes=0 gives you image embeddings.
explainer.jsNote: timm is a Python library with no official JavaScript or TypeScript package; call it from a Python service if your app is written in JavaScript.
